title: Asking questions
goal: Put the helping verb before the subject in every question
intro: In spoken Indian English, questions often keep statement order: “Why you are late?”, “Where you went?”. In standard English, a question needs a helping verb (do, does, did, is, are, have, can…) before the subject. The order is: question word + helping verb + subject + main verb.

rules.rule: Question word + helping verb + subject + verb.
No helping verb in the statement? Add do / does / did.
examples: She works here. → Does she work here?
They left. → When did they leave?

rules.rule: When the question word IS the subject, keep normal order.
examples: Who called you? (not “Who did call you?”)

mistakes.why: Add “did” and use the base form.

ex.y: Who is the subject: Who told you?
Past simple question: did she leave.

ex.q: What did happen at the meeting?
ex.y: What is the subject: What happened?

ex.a: Where did you buy that shirt?
ex.y: Question word + did + subject + base form

ex.q: Make a question with “where”: “She works in Gurgaon.”

talk: Imagine you are meeting a new colleague. Ask them six questions about their life and work, using where, what, how long, why, and do/does.
